answer: An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the nectar check immediately, the shale audit keeps the resolved set and the summit replay exposes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 160 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 160 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
